prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1469; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was operating a sedan in the center lane of a multi-lane roadway in Pasadena, Texas, and attempted to move into the adjacent lane when the right side of the vehicle made contact with the left side of a pickup truck operated by Driver 2. Driver 1 reported pain in the right knee following the impact. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 changed lanes without signaling, and two independent witnesses at the scene gave statements consistent with that account. Photographs taken at the scene show scrape marks and displaced trim along the sideswipe area of both vehicles. A passenger was seated in the front right seat of Driver 1's sedan and was confirmed present by Driver 1, Driver 2, and both witnesses. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the sedan. Officers observed no prior damage to the sedan, and none was reported by Driver 1 or Driver 2. The knee injury described is consistent with the forces expected from a side impact of this type. Some of the visible damage to the rear quarter panel of the sedan could not be clearly attributed to this impact and may require further inspection by a qualified appraiser.
